items.title: Library supplement: Hermite products of correlated Gaussian projections

source.anchor: Complete source-only.json statement and proof topology.
source.attribution: Original generic exposition of a classical Gaussian identity; existing local proof reused without a novelty or primary-textbook completion claim.

items.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\). Let \(u,v\in E\) satisfy \(\|u\|=\|v\|=1\), and put \(\rho=\langle u,v\rangle\). Let \(H_k\) denote the unnormalized probabilists’ Hermite polynomial, defined by \(H_0=1\) and \(H_{k+1}(t)=tH_k(t)-H_k^{\prime}(t)\). For every pair of natural degrees \(i,j\), the literal product \(x\mapsto H_i(\langle u,x\rangle)H_j(\langle v,x\rangle)\) is absolutely integrable under \(\gamma\). Its integral is \(i!\rho^i\) if \(i=j\), and zero if \(i\ne j\). Both degrees can be zero, and coincident or antipodal unit directions are included.
assumptions: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure; \(\gamma\) is its centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability.
\(u,v\) are actual unit vectors in the same carrier. There is no linear-independence, orthogonality or nonsingular two-dimensional density assumption.
\(i,j\in\mathbb N\) are arbitrary. The polynomials have integer coefficients evaluated in \(\mathbb R\) through the canonical coefficient map.
The correlation is the actual inner product \(\rho\in[-1,1]\). Both endpoint values and zero are allowed. Product integrability is a conclusion.

bindings.boundary: This exact integral identity does not by itself establish a full Hermite expansion, derivative bounds for a series, or an application-specific force estimate. Gaussian polynomial moments and the Stein domain are discharged in the proof, not added as public Hermite hypotheses.
